additional_requirements: The binge eating occurs, on average, at least once a week for 3 months

S049.name: Eating_Large_Amount
S049.description: Eating, in a discrete period of time, an amount of food that is definitely larger than what most individuals would eat in a similar period of time under similar circumstances.
examples: Eating more than 3-4 times the amount of a typical meal within 2 hours.
Continuously eating large amounts of high-calorie snacks in addition to main meals.
Eating enough to empty a significant portion of the refrigerator or pantry at once.
Eating clearly more food than others during the same period of time.

S050.name: Loss_of_Control
S050.description: A sense of lack of control over eating during the episode (e.g., a feeling that one cannot stop eating or control what or how much one is eating).
examples: A feeling that once I start eating, I cannot stop even if I want to.
Thinking 'I shouldn't eat any more' but mechanically continuing to eat.
A feeling of helplessness that I cannot decide for myself how much to eat.
Eating as if my body is being controlled by someone else.

S051.name: Rapid_Eating
S051.description: Eating much more rapidly than normal.
examples: Swallowing food without chewing it properly.
Eating continuously and rapidly to the point where it is difficult to breathe.
Eating so urgently that there is no time to taste the food.
Eating at a speed that surprises others.

S052.name: Eating_Until_Uncomfortably_Full
examples: Eating until the stomach feels distended to the point of bursting and pain.
Eating so much that it is difficult to even stand up or move.
Continuing to eat until feeling nauseous or like vomiting.
Unable to stop eating even though it is physically uncomfortable and painful.

S055.name: Negative_Affect_After_Binge
S055.description: Feeling disgusted with oneself, depressed, or very guilty afterward.
examples: Feeling unbearable disgust and self-loathing after binging.
Falling into extreme depression and self-criticism immediately after binging.
Feeling intense guilt and regret over the fact that I binged again.
Feeling shame that I am pathetic and have weak willpower after binging.

symptom.disease_info: Binge-Eating Disorder is characterized by recurrent episodes of consuming unusually large amounts of food within a discrete period, accompanied by a sense of loss of control over eating, occurring at least weekly for three months. Episodes are typically followed by marked distress such as shame, guilt, or disgust, but unlike bulimia nervosa, there are no regular compensatory behaviors like vomiting, fasting, or excessive exercise. The disorder often emerges in the context of dieting, weight concerns, mood or anxiety disorders, or chronic stress, and can fluctuate in severity over time. It is associated with functional impairment, medical comorbidities (e.g., obesity, metabolic syndrome), and psychosocial difficulties, and is distinguished from occasional overeating by its frequency, loss of control, and emotional impact.

patient.stressor: Magin’s shift from full-time long-haul driving to a more stationary mentorship and early transition toward fleet management changed his daily rhythm from structured routes and strict delivery windows to irregular office hours and long evenings at home alone. The routine of truck stops and timed meals was replaced with open access to his well-stocked kitchen and the comfort dishes he prided himself on perfecting, just as his youngest child moved out of state and his divorce became final. Over a three-month period, he noticed that evenings that started with cooking a simple meal after fishing or gardening would end with him standing at the stove and fridge long after he was full, using food to fill the quiet of his empty house. He finally agreed to see a clinician at his church’s urging when he mentioned in small group that he was embarrassed by how much he was eating alone at night and felt his relationship with food had become something he was hiding rather than sharing.
patient.chief_complaint: I keep eating in the evenings until I’m so full it’s uncomfortable, even when I don’t really want more.

S049.name: Eating_Large_Amount
S049.description: Eating, in a discrete period of time, an amount of food that is definitely larger than what most individuals would eat in a similar period of time under similar circumstances.
S049.manifestation: These nights at home, I’ll cook a normal dinner, but then I just keep going—leftover roast, half a loaf of bread, a big bowl of cereal, ice cream straight from the tub—way more than anyone I’ve ever driven with would eat in one sitting, and it’s all gone before I realize it.

S050.name: Loss_of_Control
S050.description: A sense of lack of control over eating during the episode (e.g., a feeling that one cannot stop eating or control what or how much one is eating).
S050.manifestation: Once I start picking at the food in the kitchen after supper, it’s like something takes over and I’m watching myself grab one thing after another even while I’m telling myself, ‘Magin, stop, you don’t need this,’ and I just don’t stop until it’s all gone or I’m hurting.

S051.name: Rapid_Eating
S051.description: Eating much more rapidly than normal.
S051.manifestation: I eat so fast in those moments that I’m barely chewing—standing at the counter shoveling in cold leftovers and slices of cheese like I’m on a tight delivery window again, only there’s no deadline, just me and the food disappearing before I’ve even tasted it.

S052.name: Eating_Until_Uncomfortably_Full
S052.manifestation: Most evenings now I’ll keep eating past the point where I feel full, to where my belly is stretched and tight and I have to lean back in the recliner and unbuckle my belt because it’s uncomfortable to move, but I still had a few more bites anyway even though I didn’t want them.

S055.name: Negative_Affect_After_Binge
S055.description: Feeling disgusted with oneself, depressed, or very guilty afterward.
S055.manifestation: After one of those nights, I sit there in the quiet house staring at the dirty dishes and empty containers, feeling gross, ashamed, and beating myself up that a grown man who used to run whole routes on a schedule can’t even control what he puts in his own mouth.

add_requirements.binge_frequency: Ever since I stopped long-haul runs and started this mentorship role, these big evening eating spells have been happening pretty much every night, at least several times a week without any real break.
add_requirements.functional_impairment: I’ve started turning down invites to grab dinner or watch the game with buddies from the yard because I’m embarrassed about how I eat at night and feel worn out and sluggish the next morning at work after stuffing myself.
add_requirements.duration: This has really been a problem for about the last three months, starting around when my divorce was finalized and I shifted from the road to more of the office and mentoring work.
